interest: Although consisting solely of a List of Papers docket sheet, this file illustrates the State Department's decimal filing and cross-referencing practices for colonial economic intelligence in East Asia prior to World War II. It highlights American diplomatic surveillance of Japanese imperial economic development and capital flows in colonial Taiwan (Formosa) via consular reporting from Taihoku by Foreign Service Officer John K. Emmerson. Crucially for historians, it serves as an archival roadmap directing researchers to file 894a.50/11 for the substantive report on Japanese capital penetration on the eve of the Pacific War.
overview: This file (894.503194A) consists of a single State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet recording documentation on the investment and field of investment of Japanese capital in Formosa (Taiwan). The sheet contains a single docket entry referencing an unnumbered report dated December 4, 1939, from John K. Emmerson at Taihoku (Taipei). A purport note directs researchers to decimal file 894a.50/11, indicating that the substantive report on Japanese capital in Taiwan was catalogued and filed under that related classification rather than retained physically within this dossier.

subfiles.summary: This single-page List of Papers docket sheet for decimal file 894.503194A records an incoming dispatch or report regarding the investment of Japanese capital in Formosa (Taiwan). The entry records a document dated December 4, 1939, originating from consular officer John K. Emmerson at Taihoku. The accompanying purport note indicates that the substantive report was filed under classification 894a.50/11, leaving this sheet as an index marker for archival reference.
